title: Phase 1 shared run-level prompt prefix: can a byte-stable family prefix make 25% of uncached worker input tokens cacheable?
summary: Hypothesis: A shared, byte-stable run-level prompt prefix (identical for all nodes of the same role family) reorders the prompt to put cross-family blocks before family-specific blocks, making the prefix cacheable under provider automatic token caching. This should make at least 25% of Orchestrator-written uncached worker input tokens cacheable, with no rule lost. Method: Deterministic synthetic comparison. Rendered 14 calls (4 implementer, 2 test_author, 1 repairer, 6 reviewer, 1 planner) of one synthetic run with the shared_prefix flag off and on, using fixed project state and per-node worktrees. Modelled provider automatic prefix caching at token granularity (longest common prefix with any earlier prompt of the same family). Variant: shared_prefix flag on in prompts.build_measured(). Outcome: The shared_prefix variant reduces total uncached input tokens from 17,637 to 13,709 (22.27% reduction ratio). For worker input only, uncached tokens fall from 10,553 to 6,625 (37.22% reduction ratio). Cache-read share improves from 0.8822 to 0.9261 for workers. Parity held: all rule sections present in both variants, no rules lost. Promotion gate: (1) noninferior validation: existing tests must pass unchanged with the flag; currently blocked by test failure in `test_orchestrator_telemetry.EngineTelemetryTests.test_context_selection_is_recorded_for_registered_projects` (candidate_tokens_estimate missing from prefix event). (2) Lower cost per verified task on real runs: requires `orchestrate context-economy` re-measurement on live runs with flag=True. Interpretation: The pre-registered falsifier (overall uncached_ratio 0.2227 < 0.25) was triggered, so the hypothesis is not met. The secondary fixture measurement on worker input only (37.22% reduction) shows stronger benefit for individual workers, but this is subordinate to the overall measurement. The result is modelled on token-granular automatic caching; real delivery depends on provider caching capability and adapter support (Claude style requires explicit cache block, outside Phase 1 scope). Current default: False until validation gate passes.
